issue_title: Debugging "process has died" errors on startup or segmentation fault
issue_contents: This post is about ROS1. For **ROS2**, see this post below https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap_ros/issues/28#issuecomment-1336292967
Before continuing, make sure `xterm` and `gdb` are installed:
Before rebuilding source or in Debug mode (**B**,**C**), launch the crashing node in [gdb](http://wiki.ros.org/roslaunch/Tutorials/Roslaunch%20Nodes%20in%20Valgrind%20or%20GDB).
If using `rtabmap` or `rgbd_odometry` nodes directly in your launch file, we can add the `launch-prefix` like that:

When the node crashes, type `bt` (backtrace). If the log contains **Eigen** stuff, see this [comment](https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap_ros/issues/239#issuecomment-385064255) about `-march=native` compilation flag problem.
If you are using the binaries (e.g., ros-indigo-rtabmap and ros-indigo-rtabmap-ros):
If the nodes are still crashing, go to **B**.
If **A** doesn't work, clean up your catkin workspace and build rtabmap in Debug mode:
When an error comes up, you can use `backtrace` (or simply `bt`) command in gdb to show more info.
issue_code: roslaunch rtabmap_ros rtabmap.launch launch_prefix:="xterm -e gdb -ex run --args"
<node pkg="rtabmap_ros" type="rgbd_odometry" name="rgbd_odometry" launch-prefix="xterm -e gdb -ex run --args">
<node pkg="rtabmap_ros" type="rtabmap" name="rtabmap" launch-prefix="xterm -e gdb -ex run --args">
$ roslaunch rtabmap_ros rgbd_mapping.launch launch_prefix:="xterm -e gdb -ex run --args"
contents_details: Install `rtabmap` and `rtabmap_ros` from source following this [instructions](https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap_ros#build-from-source).
Clean your catkin workspace (assuming your catkin workspace is `~/catkin_ws`, just keep `src` folder):

Now, if rtabmap is still crashing, start the [launch file with gdb](http://wiki.ros.org/roslaunch/Tutorials/Roslaunch%20Nodes%20in%20Valgrind%20or%20GDB) to track down where it is crashing (make sure you have the latest version of [rgbd_mapping.launch](https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap_ros/blob/master/launch/rgbd_mapping.launch) with `launch_prefix` argument):
[Open an issue](https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap_ros/issues/new) here with the log of gdb for the nodes crashing and with which kind of computer you are using.

issue_contents: Due to PR #66 some misconfigured costmap settings has been identified.

issue_title: global exotica seed
issue_contents: I added a `KinematicTree::SetSeed` method in https://github.com/ipab-slmc/exotica/pull/487 to allow reproducible sampling of configurations.

A call to `KinematicTree::BuildTree` resets the random number generator: https://github.com/ipab-slmc/exotica/blob/7905a390e1b88ef58c7ad4f418983bdf303b21d5/exotica_core/src/kinematic_tree.cpp#L283 and requires to set the seed again.
Q1: Is this reset of the `generator_` required? Can it be removed or should we replace `rd_()` by the user set seed?

I think it would be good if EXOTica would keep a global seed for all random number generator that may be used in solvers, tasks, etc., to enable reproducible results and easier debugging. This seed would be determined once at the beginning and all random number generators would need to use the same seed, e.g. an `exotica::seed()` that either returns a random or static user chosen seed.
Q2: Does this sound feasible? What would be a good approach to make sure that all random number generators use the same seed?

issue_title: Required and Optional parameters in initialiser
issue_contents: The initialiser definition supports `Required` and `Optional` parameters.
What is the intended behaviour of those?

The `Optional` can be used with and without default argument (set via `=`). `Required` on the other hand does not support default arguments but the Initializer can be constructed without providing an argument value, in which case it is using random memory.
I think the `Required` and `Optional` properties should be implicitly defined by a default argument:
contents_details: if no default argument is given, the parameter is `Required` and the initialiser should throw an error if no argument is provided.
contents_details_more: if a default argument is set via `=`, the parameter is `Optional`

issue_title: AICO/BayesianIK without damping broken (NaN)

The underlying reason is our inversion assumes a *positive-definite* matrix, but `Sinv` is all zeros.

issue_title: Serialization
Proper support for multi-timestep or trajectory cost terms
issue_contents: We are currently updating the time steps one by one even when solvers are evaluating entire trajectories. This update logic prevents us from correctly applying Jacobians over multiple timesteps. The transition cost is a special case which is handled _separately_ but we have more, similar use cases that would benefit from a trajectory update.
contents_details: Then, update all task maps with a new trajectory update method. This one will default to running a for loop within the taskmap with the single step call back if it does not exist.
contents_details_more: Finally, update the cost and constraints

issue_title: TaskMap is_used logic insufficient for trajectories
issue_contents: Currently, lazy updating of task maps uses a `is_used` flag that is updated via the `UpdateS` call of the `EndPoseTask`/`TimeIndexedTask`/`SamplingTask`.
This is OK for end pose problems.

This is insufficient for trajectories: If we use a taskmap only in one or a few timesteps, it will still get updated over the entire trajectory. This doesn't matter for inexpensive taskmaps but heavily for expensive ones.
Ideally, the `is_used` should be time-indexed as well and move from the `TaskMap` class to the `Tasks` classes.

issue_title: Convention for constraints: Rho and fixed offsets
issue_contents: Our current implementation of constraints suffers from a few flaws:
contents_details: "Flipping" an inequality constraint using Rho=-1 often breaks the problem and solver. Our default Snopt examples exhibit this, for instance.
The tasks compute `S * ydiff <= 0`, where the constant part is already subtracted. Some solvers benefit from explicitly specifying the constant part (such that `A*x = -b` instead of `A*x+b=0`

issue_title: Cast dynamically loaded plugins to derived class to access non-virtual functions
issue_contents: Noticed while writing a unit test for a task map:
contents_details: We load taskmaps (and many other things) as plugins where most of the relevant functions are provided via polymorphism (virtual in the interface, override in the derived class).
However, some taskmaps require explicit additional methods that are not part of the interface but only in the derived class (`getPoint`, `setPoint`, `SetPreviousJointState`).
In C++, when we load (via `pluginlib` -> `class_loader` -> `libpoco-dev`), we cannot cast the pointer of a taskmap (`Taskmap_ptr`) to its derived type to access the derived-only methods.
contents_details_more: This works fine in the Python module as it is compiled with all the source files.

issue_title: OMPL path simplification leads to collisions for high-DoF systems
issue_contents: After eliminating a few other factors (e.g. impact of "Range" on validity check between two states) it is clear that path simplification that we turn on by default eliminates required vertices and leads to paths that are in collision. To even obtain a valid plan in the first place, ``Range`` (the distance between two states among which connectivity can be established) needs to be set _very low_, much lower than the value automatically detected by OMPL.
Setting RangeRatio / InterpolationLength / SnapToVertex to different values does not resolve the problem.

The source of this is not taking into account the first timestep (for task cost), which we aren't changing in most cases. This reduces comparability of cost across solvers - ideally we should perform roll-outs within the problem to avoid this problem in the first place.

issue_title: StartState convention and treatment for controlled subgroups
issue_contents: We just resolved this with a workaround for @cmower but should look into why it occurs. It occurs when the ControlledJoints are a subset of the ModelJoints. The start state should be able to be set as only a vector of the size of the controlled joints _or_ or a vector of the size of the model joints. However, when first setting the uncontrolled joints and then setting the start state with a vector of only the controlled joints the uncontrolled joints are reset to zero.
We should (a) add a unit test and (b) fix the convention.
It's likely a super quick fix and I'll come back to it after the deadlines.

**Issue 2:** The ``KinematicTree::publishFrames`` publishes the non-padded/scaled shapes. This may be fine since padding and scaling is a CollisionScene-internal thing, but should be noted.

**Issue 3:** PlanningScene messages that are extracted from Scene (e.g. to be published for visualization or passed to other planners) do not have the padding reflected. A fix for this is in progress.

issue_title: rosbagを再生してもcamera_linkへのtfが出ない
issue_contents: 最近，[hrp2_record.launch](https://github.com/jsk-ros-pkg/jsk_common/blob/master/jsk_data/launch/hrp2_record.launch) で取ったrosbagをlocalで再生してもpointcloudがrvizに表示されない問題が起こっていました．
BODY（またはground）からcamera_rgb_optical_frameなどへのtfが参照できないのがその原因で，
で確認すると確かにHEAD_LINK1からcamera_linkへのtfが出ていませんでした．
@mmurooka @pazeshun に協力してもらい調べた結果，
先日ロボット体内のPCをindigoからkineticにupdateしたタイミングで，
staticなtfは```/tf_static```として，最初の1回しかpublishされなくなっており，
結果rosbagにも保存されなくなっていたということがわかりました．
現状の解決策としては，
ロボットを起動するときに立ち上げるlaunchファイル内でpublishしている該当する[static tf](https://github.com/start-jsk/rtmros_hrp2/blob/master/jsk_hrp2_ros_bridge/launch/hrp2017_local.launch#L24-L27)を，
localでrosbagを再生するときにも自前でpublishすることで対処しています．
他に良い解決策はあるでしょうか．

issue_title: 複数ロボットを組み合わせてロボットを作る方法
issue_contents: 複数のロボットを組み合わせて、一台のロボットを作ったときの
_ri_と_robot_の定義をどうしましょうか、というチケットです。
例えば、アーム単体で動くロボットと台車単体で動くロボットを
組み合わせてロボットを作る、という状況です。
としたときに、何も考えずにコードを書くと、
同じようなコードを二つのファイルにかくことになります。
もちろん、joint_statesなど二つのロボットでバッティングしそうな
ところはうまくかくか、調停してあげる必要がありますが、
そうでなくて丸コピできるところをどうしたらよいか、というのが動機です。
実はハンドをつける、というようなのにも
関わってくる問題かもしれません。
２とおりくらい試して見ましたが、何かもっと良い方法があれば
コメントもらえると助かります。
のようにして、defmethodに書いてあるようなことをdefunにしておいて、
のようにしてdefmethodをevalする、という方法です。
アーム＋台車ロボットの中で、arm-robotというスロット変数をつくっておいて、
みたいなもので、:init-endingあたりで
がevalされるという方法です。
それぞれ、メリットデメリットがあったきがしますが、
このあたりのコードをどっと書いていてド忘れてしまったので、
思い出したらまた書きます。

issue_title: openraveで変換したcolladaファイルが読めない
issue_contents: openrave xmlからopenraveを使って、コマンドでcolladaファイルに変換できる。
変換したcollada fileは、jsk-ros-pkgのcollada関連プログラムで正しく読み込むことができない。
euscolladaのcollada2eusではプログラムは終了するが、ジオメトリだけできて、ロボットモデルが生成されない。
collada_toolsのcollada_to_urdfではSegfaultする。こちらは、collada_parserのレベルでSegfaultするようだ。
をvisual_scene内で参照してつくっているノードのインスタンス
があるが、これを、参照ではなくlibrary_nodes内のノードをコピーして実体とすると、正しく変換される。
colladaの仕様としては、変換されないファイルも正しいと思われるので、プログラムを修正して
変換できるようにするべき。

issue_title: optmotiongenにおけるbsplineを用いたdynamicな動作について
PR2でOptmotiongenの障害物回避IKが上手くいかない
issue_contents: Optmotiongenの[sample-arm-reach-ik-obstacle](https://github.com/jsk-ros-pkg/jsk_control/tree/master/eus_qp/optmotiongen#sample-arm-reach-ik-obstacle)に使われている障害物回避IKをPR2で試してみようとした(https://github.com/Kanazawanaoaki/oneweek_kanazawa/issues/1 )ところ以下のような問題が発生しました。
sample-arm-reach-ik-obstacleと同じように`:obstacles (list *obstacle*)`として障害物を指定してもPR2の場合は障害物回避をすることが出来ませんでした。

@pazeshunに`:obstacles (list *obstacle*)`の代わりに`:collision-avoidance-link-pair (mapcar #'(lambda (l) (list l *obstacle*)) (send *robot* :links))`とする必要があることを教えていただきましたが、[README](https://github.com/jsk-ros-pkg/jsk_control/blob/master/eus_qp/optmotiongen/README.md )から辿るにはPR2のregraspの[サンプルのコード](https://github.com/jsk-ros-pkg/jsk_control/blob/master/eus_qp/optmotiongen/euslisp/demo/demo-pr2-regrasp-object.l )を注意深く読む以外にない気がします。
(https://gist.github.com/Kanazawanaoaki/1810958f83c44c037b9cb286a047b385#file-obstacle-ik-test-02-l )のように`:collision-avoidance-link-pair`を指定して実行してみたのですが、障害物を回避しきれていなくて障害物と重なってしまっているように見えます。
`(normal-ik)`として`:inverse-kinematics`を使った時と、`(obstacle-ik)`として`:inverse-kinematics-optmotiongen`を使った時の挙動を比べると障害物を指定できていて回避していようとしているように見えます。完全には回避しきれない状態で解き終わってしまうこともあるのでしょうか。

issue_title: :angle-vector内の:angle-vector-durationに関して
issue_contents: :angle-vector内の:angle-vector-durationに関して、先週@itohdakと見ていてふと思ったのですが、
で:angle-vector-durationの部分で「あまり速く動きすぎないようにする」目的で:potentio-vectorを使ってると思いますが、
これは:reference-vectorでなくて良いでしょうか。

rtmros_commonのロボットでは、:angle-vectorはSequencePlayerに届き（値が:reference-vectorに保持されます）、その後その値がimpedanceController、Stabilizer、CollisionDetectorなど、センサフィードバック、フェイルセーフ用制御器が関節角値を上がいています（これが実機に送られ、エンコーダ値にでてくる最終結果が:potentio-vectorになります）。
などの理由から、:reference-vectorが良いようにも思いました。
:potentio-vectorが良いか、:reference-vectorが良いか、はもしかしたらロボットや状況によって違うかもしれなくて議論がいるかもしれないです。
ちなみに以下でrtmros_commonでは再現します
なお、関節角度を少し速めて送りたい（短い時間で送りたい）ときに問題なるかと思ってましたが、
誤って:angle-vectorの引数の:min-timeを1.0秒のままにしてチェックしてたので、
:potentio-vectorで計算される時間があまり大きくなく、あまり問題でないかもしれないです。

issue_title: Error messages from rviz plugin if slightly different timestamps on jsk_recognition_msgs::BoundingBox and jsk_recognition_msgs::BoundingBoxArray
issue_contents: when visualising `jsk_recognition_msgs::BoundingBoxArray` messages in rviz I get a continuous stream of errors like:

I am running with `use_sim_time` set to true but for some reason the error is referring to the simtime header timestamp and walltime. but there is not problem if I check the transform with `tf_echo` etc.  The box actually displays fine, as expected, but the stream of errors and "status:error " isn't nice. Example of a message that triggers this error: (note a difference in the `nsecs` field)

issue_title: CI failures due to test data download failures after Google Drive's change
issue_contents: It seems the full test on noetic in CI fails always recently.
I think this is because of the change of Google Drive's sharing permissions and that disables the download of test data from Google Drive as the following. Previously the sign-in was not required.

We upload files and download them from [JSK_public_data](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/0B9P1L--7Wd2vUGplQkVLTFBWcFE?resourcekey=0-qlPyB_oRQm887pgRGiPhgg), so **ideally** the permission should be
We couldn't find a way of how to make it writable only for people in JSK, so we have been using
But now, Google Drive has changed its specification and **config-actual** won't work anymore (as it requires sign-in even for just downloading files via links).

I think the solution would be adding a group to JSK_public_data that includes all members in JSK (something like jsk-all-members@jsk.imi.i.u-tokyo.ac.jp). Please let me know if there's already such group (maybe it would be better to let me know via email not to make it public).

issue_title: euslisp dependency in roseus
issue_contents: I ran into this trying to get the jsk stacks to build in [my ros-o buildfarm](https://github.com/v4hn/ros-o-builder).

[roseus find_packages euslisp](https://github.com/jsk-ros-pkg/jsk_roseus/blob/fa36ffdc4fe2c9c581127bbc1e36be62ddc15f02/roseus/CMakeLists.txt#L54), but the [*upstream* euslisp package](https://github.com/euslisp/EusLisp) does not provide a cmake config upon installation, so building against debian's own `euslisp-dev` package fails for no real reason. [Your eulisp-release package](https://github.com/tork-a/euslisp-release) of course provides a package.xml and bloom will autogenerate a cmake config for it, which is why it works with the bloomed package in the ros ecosystem.

To follow ROS-best-practices, you should not rely on anything that is not available in upstream packages when using external packages packaged in ROS. The rest of the roseus CMakeLists.txt relies on multiple variables that are set through that cmake config, so I'm unsure how you can get rid of it. (I'm not using euslisp at all).
In Ubuntu 22.04 euslisp is at version 9.27 and you packaged 9.29 in noetic. Are there important differences for which you need the ros-packaged version?

issue_title: roseus is almost 30x slower than irteusgl when testing transparent.l
issue_contents: When testing https://github.com/euslisp/jskeus/blob/master/irteus/test/transparent.l with the current opt version:
This is due to having the misfortune of landing in a situation in which there is not enough heap memory available, so the gc runs many unnecessary times.

Usually the heap memory is resized to `totalheap * gcmargin` to avoid this issue. However, in this case it happens that enough memory is allocated in the first gc attempt, so the heap is never resized.

issue_title: Memory faults on subscribers
issue_contents: I have been struggling with weird segfaults on my custom build for some time but I believe I have finally found a way to reproduce them in the release build:
This will execute normally at first but eventually cause a segmentation fault if ran for long enough.
Testing with the  1.7.4-1bionic.20210505.033302 and  1.7.4-1bionic.20200930.061900 builds several times the segmentation fault occurred around 900, 2400 and 8600 iterations, depending on each run.

The subscribers registered in this case look something like `(#<compiled-code #X5610a667fe40 send> #<my-sub #X5610a6cdb6c8> :update)` and are attributed to symbols in the lisp package to avoid being garbage collected.
However, I believe that the object instances within the registered and supposedly guarded list are actually succeptible to being garbage collected, leading to the observed segmentation faults.
I have also verified that the errors always occur just after a garbage collection.
@708yamaguchi Could you see if you can recreate the situation in your machine?

issue_title: Configurable z-index for overlays?
issue_contents: Hi, thanks a lot for the visualization plugins you made. I really love all the overlay plugins. I'm not that familiar with 3D rendering and Ogre, so I can't figure out a pull request myself. It would really be nice to be able to configure z-index of the overlays, so that if they overlap, the order in which they are rendered is given (currently, it seems to me the order is random). There could either be a configuration value for the z-index, or it could at least be given by the order of the overlays in the Displays view (i.e. the closer to the end of the list, the higher z-index).

issue_title: Action dispatch only when previous action is complete for non-durative actions
issue_contents: I wanted to ask for some clarification regarding the esteral-plan dispatcher.

I noticed that for non-durative operators, all actions are being dispatched at the same time, even if the previous action has not finished. Another thing is that there are no edges between action1_END --> action2_START of two consecutive action nodes action1 and action2 but only between the two start nodes action1_Start --> action2_START.
Is there any way to enforce dispatching of actions only when the previous one has finished, even when using non-durative pddl operators?

issue_title: Refactor rosplan_dependencies CMakeLists
issue_contents: As done for CHIMP in #274, it would be good to only compile some dependencies when needed by the user (i.e. by using some flags).
We could also go further and only checkout submodules when they are needed and do that in the CMakeLists. That will make rosplan cloning a bit faster (though the first compilation could be slower).

The "makeInitialState()" method of "PDDLProblemGenerator" writes parameters of a predicate following the order in which they are stored in KB, but this is wrong. And same problem is happening in "makeGoals()". The parameters of a predicate could be stored in any order in the KB because they have name, but the problem file generated is wrong due to this assumption.

As this is is not happening in the old version of ROSPlan, I have compared both codes. The makeInitialState() in the new version of ROSPlan is:

Same code could be found in "makeGoals()" of old version of ROSPlan.
Therefore, my conclusion is that this is a bug. Please, could someone confirm it? Thanks.

issue_title: Tool_pose information and cartesian_client_control API in gazebo simulation
issue_contents: Hello dear researchers! I faced the question that I want to obtain both the **tool_pose information** and **cartesian_client_control API** in gazebo simulation, which can be easily accessible with real Kinova jaco robots. I started the jaco 2 robotic arm in the simulation and did not find the corresponding ros-topic/service for tool position and position control on the physical arm? Is there any support for this? If so, please let me know, thanks!

issue_title: Issues about the practical trajectory
issue_contents: When I used the MoveIt to do path planning of kinova j2n6s200, the practical trajectory cannot move according to the planned one,  it seems that the inverse kinematics cannot show the right joint values for the practical kinova j2n6s200.

issue_title: End-effector Force Control behaviour Issue
issue_contents: We have a question about End-effector Force Control behaviour on our Kinova Jaco2 j2n6s300 arm & noetic-devel kinova-ros.

Our experiment set up is quite simple, we have a small box (180gms) gripped by the arm. We apply a constant end-effector force in the +z direction by continuously pumping kinova_msgs.msg.CartesianForce messages into the *_driver/in/cartesian_force topic in torque_control mode. Our expectation was that the box would be lifted up with a constant acceleration/linearly increasing velocity with position changes only in +z axis all the way till the arm periphery is reached as long as the applied force is larger than what is required to overcome weight of the box 1.8N.

However we found the behaviour different in the following ways and was wondering if you could provide some guidance. Attached pdfs a few graphs of expected (from a basic simulation) and actual trajectories with the arm
Just wondering if you could help us understand this behaviour or if it is a bug; perhaps it is something basic that we are overlooking ?
The code we use is very similar to the publishForceCmd method from
Branch and commit you are using :  https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/tree/noetic-devel
contents_details: The position changes (from any initial state) reaches a steady state instead of increasing continuously till the force applied ends.
While the acceleration and velocity of the end-effector increases for higher values of forces (as expected), but they quickly come back down to 0 even though the force continues to be applied
Although we are applying force only in the +z direction, we can see motion and change in the end-effector force values (measured from *_driver/out/tool_wrench.force) in x,y & z direction

On applying cartesian_force [0, 0, +ft, 0, 0, 0], via cartesian_force topic we were expecting the current *_driver/out/tool_wrench.force values to be increased by approximately the same amount. But we could not find any discernible relation b/w those.

issue_title: MoveIt demo with Gazebo and j2s7s300
issue_contents: The following code runs moveit with the Gazebo model for robot j2s7s300 (7 dof robot with a spherical wrist)
the planning in moveit fails every time with this warning:

[ WARN] [1525102790.308848354, 63.185000000]: Joint 'j2s7s300_joint_6' from the starting state is outside bounds by a significant margin: [ 7.4013 ] should be in the range [ 1.13446 ], [ 5.14872 ] but the error above the ~start_state_max_bounds_error parameter (currently set to 0.1)

Indeed, when we monitor the joint_states topic /j2s7s300/joint_states, you see that joint 6 is at 7.401301704590916, which is outside of its limits. I could not find much information on this error in gazebo, but it seems it might be related to an instability or something when the robot get's spawned.

I first tried to modify the controllers of the 7 dof robot [here ](https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/blob/master/kinova_control/config/j2s7s300_control.yaml), but nothing would do. Then I tried to change the [urdf file ](https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/blob/master/kinova_description/urdf/j2s7s300.xacro) and change the angle limits on joint 6. I was very surprised to see that if I am more tolerant on the limits e.g.
the robot was then spawned with angle 6 inside the limits. I do not get this exact behaviour....

The thing is, the real Kinova 7 dof robot with a spherical wrist has angle limits 65-295 degree on joint 6 for safety reasons. Changing the limits for this actuator in the urdf file means the gazebo model as well as the planning in moveit will not be really representative of the real robot's capabilities. Then, I tried to modify the frames orientation so the zero position on joint 6 in the urdf is when link5 and link6 form a straight line. This corresponds to 180 degree on joint 6 on the real robot.
The changes in the urdf file were the following:

I also modified the start up position in [move_robot.py](https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/blob/master/kinova_control/src/move_robot.py) from moveJoint ([0.0,2.9,0.0,1.3,4.2,1.4,0.0],prefix,nbJoints) to moveJoint ([0.0,2.9,0.0,1.3,1.5,**-1.8**,2.0],prefix,nbJoints) to take into account joint 6's new "zero position"

This is a working solution, but it requires to change what is published by [kinova_arm.cpp](https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/blob/4ebae0119eb9ae5636e4ef8718c18415a78ba9b2/kinova_driver/src/kinova_arm.cpp) on j2s7s300_driver/out/joint_angles for joint 6, and possibly [kinova_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp](https://github.com/Kinovarobotics/kinova-ros/blob/master/kinova_driver/src/kinova_joint_trajectory_controller.cpp).
I wondered if anyone has already experienced any issues with Gazebo not respecting joint limits given in the urdf at spawning? If so, let us know

issue_title: libcurl4 dependency issue between gazebo and raptor
issue_contents: When using the toyota hsrb (which is used by the suturo project), you install some packages, including `libgazebo11-dev` which depends on `libcurl4-openssl-dev`. However `libraptor2-dev`, which is required for knowrob, depends on `libcurl4-gnutls-dev`.
These two packages conflict with each other (the both provide header files for libcurl-ssl), so you can't use the hsrb packages and knowrob together.
As a temporary fix i repackaged the libraptor2-dev package with a dependency on the more general `libcurl-ssl-dev`.
This works, but it is not clean.
contents_details: create an empty dummy package for `libcurl4-openssl-dev` to satisfy the dependency of `libpraptor2-dev` (optionally this dummy package depends on a real implementation)

issue_title: Questions about BasicLaserOdometry
issue_contents: I have a question about the implementation of BasicLaserOdometry.

My understanding is that `_transform` represents the relative transformation between the current point cloud and the previous point cloud (both are projected to the start of the current sweep), and it needs to be initialized to zero before performing Gauss-Newton optimization.

But it seems that `_transform` is not initialized to zero in `BasicLaserOdometry::process()`, and instead its position is subtracted by `_imuVeloFromStart * _scanPeriod`. I would like to know the reason for this. Thank you!

issue_title: Question about relSweepTime and _imuPositionShift
issue_contents: A question about these two variables. Please correct me if I am wrong. The **relSweepTime**, from my understanding, is the current time relative to the sweep start time, as calculated by toSec(_scanTime - _sweepStart) + relTime; **relTime** is the point time stamp relative to the scan start time. However, when calculating the **_ImuPositionShift**, the _imuPositionShift = _imuCur.position - _imuStart.position - _imuStart.velocity * relSweepTime indicates that the **_imuStart**(which is the IMU state at scan start time) is multiplied by the **relSweepTime**. It results in: velocity from a scan start * time duration from a sweep start to current. Why is it not **_imuStart.velocity * relTime**? It is a velocity from a scan start * time duration from a scan start to current.

issue_title: Illegal C++ Identifiers
issue_contents: The code uses the convention of naming members with an `_` prefix:  `_memberName`.
Such names are [_"are reserved and may not be declared in a program, doing so invokes **undefined behavior**"_](http://en.cppreference.com/w/c/language/identifier).
Such members should be renamed to e.g. `memberName_`.
Actually, _members_ starting with `_` are technically OK, but are[ generally  frowned upon](https://stackoverflow.com/a/3651336/135862), because they may lead to erroneously using UB forms:
issue_quotes: 1. identifiers starting with an underscore, followed by a capital character
2. identifiers having two consecutive underscores anywhere
3. identifiers in the global namespace starting with an underscore
... Rather than trying to remember these rules, many simply do not use identifiers starting with an underscore. That's why the trailing underscore was invented.

issue_title: Point interpolation error
issue_contents: I'm currently trying to improve the implementation of this algorithm. As part of my refactorings, I changed the calculation of the ring start and end indices. They are now calculated by accumulating the sizes of the individual ring clouds. After doing so, I noticed a slight difference in the results and took a closer look again.
after line 384 in scanRegistration.cpp to output the scanCount variable each time it changes.
While for some scans, the output matches the expected sequence, namely:
some other scans show the following output:

As a result, the calculated scan start and end indices are sometimes not corresponding to the actual scan ring indices in the combined cloud. This even sometimes results in the scenario where the start index of the last ring is grater than its end index (since the end index is set explicitly afterwards).

The problem seems to originate in the calculation of the relative time of a point based on its angle, respectively the determination of the start and end angles. Tests have shown that (for a VLP-16) the scan range per received input cloud is slightly more than 360 degrees. This in combination with other issues in determining the start and end orientation probably produces negative relative time values, causing the point to "hop" to its predecessor ring.
This issue translates over to the lidarOdometry component, as it also uses the intensities of the points. However, I'm not sure yet about its implications there.
After fixing the scan start and end index calculation, the overall result is comparable, but slightly different. I can't tell if it's better or worse, yet.

issue_title: Request to Add Support for YUV Format in visp_bridge
issue_contents: I encountered an issue when using `usb_cam` to launch my Logitech camera(C9xx) and converting the ROS image to ViSP format with `visp_bridge`. The converted image appears distorted.
This limitation is similar to the issue discussed in [ros2/common_interfaces #76](https://github.com/ros2/common_interfaces/issues/76).
Upon reviewing the `visp_bridge` source code, I noticed it does not support the YUV format.

Could you consider adding support for this format in `visp_bridge`? I suggest incorporating the YUV422_YUY2 format specifically. This addition would align `visp_bridge` with the capabilities of [sensor_msgs](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/p/sensor_msgs/generated/file__tmp_ws_src_common_interfaces_sensor_msgs_include_sensor_msgs_image_encodings.hpp.html), the [vpImageConvert Class](https://visp-doc.inria.fr/doxygen/visp-daily/classvpImageConvert.html), and [usb_cam](https://github.com/ros-drivers/usb_cam/tree/ros2), all of which support the YUV422_YUY2 format.
Would it be acceptable for me to create a Pull Request to introduce this feature, or would you prefer to implement it differently?
Below is a proposed implementation snippet for handling YUV422_YUY2 format images in the toVispImageRGBa function:

issue_contents: What is the reason for overwriting the frame_id in the header of the PoseStamped message for in line 194 - 196 of node.cpp of the vision_auto_tracker?

The `tracker_ref_frame` is set to "\map" in names.cpp which overwrites whatever frame the image (and therefore the pose calculated) used as a reference. The same is also done to the covariance position.

issue_title: Slow detections because a detection image is generated even when there are no subscribers
issue_contents: On these [lines](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/darknet_ros/blob/1027a2806712918eea967da02f12c3d8c95af9db/darknet_ros/src/YoloObjectDetector.cpp#L505-L507) the detection image is generated and significantly slows down the detection speed since it is copying pixels in an image with a for loop. This doesn't need to occur at this stage and can be moved after it is checked if anyone is subscribing to the detection topic ([here](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/darknet_ros/blob/1027a2806712918eea967da02f12c3d8c95af9db/darknet_ros/src/YoloObjectDetector.cpp#L243)).
The detection image should not be generated unless there are subscribers.
I've tested this locally on a fork of PR #319. It increases the FPS from a max of 120 to 150, along with the average FPS being higher.

issue_title: CPU real-time testing problem
issue_contents: Hello, i'm testing Yolov2-tiny only on CPU (also set GPU = 0),  both on bag files and real time camera streams.
At first I cloned the [leggedrobotics repo](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/darknet_ros) which resulted in asynchronized messages between the bounding boxes and detection images.

Issue posts (again) led me [here](https://github.com/MayurT/darknet_ros/tree/fix/action_server_result). This version of YoloObjectDetector.cpp actually bypassed the asynchronization.
By modifying .cfg file, Im testing the detector on **320*320 network input resolution** which results almost in **~1 FPS** on **Intel i7-8565u CPU @ 1,8GHz × 8**.
**Q1:** Any rational explanation for bag files initial synchronization solution , not working for real time streams?
**Q3:** Can FPS increase be achieved without modifying the network's input image resolution (which I know that works)?
**Q4:** OpenMP = 1 or 0 inside /darknet_ros/darknet/Makefile seems to not affect the FPS. Is this really how Multithreading is enabled?

issue_title: Last image stuck in detection loop
issue_contents: When testing darknet_ros with recorded rosbags, we encounter the following problem:

There will be no message like "Waiting for image" since the [while-block](https://github.com/leggedrobotics/darknet_ros/blob/master/darknet_ros/src/YoloObjectDetector.cpp#L510) will be not left, unless the rosnode is closed - which is not.

This beaviour is very bad. We use several cameras but it can happen that at some time no camera is recording, so darknet would do inference on the last image. Thus, it will alway publish the same bounding boxes until new images arrive.
Did anyone else encounter this problem? How can you fix the node, so that if no new image arrives, darknet just prints "Waiting for image" and only waits?
contents_details: Running darknet rosnode is fine, the net will be initialized and then the message "Waiting for image" will be printed.
As soon as I run the rosbag, darknet receives the image and does the inference and publishes the messages as it should
contents_details_more: When I stop the rosbag, than darknet will always run the net on the last received image in loop.

issue_title: Add maximum error limit to robot matching
issue_contents: When matching robots to detected robots in the vision system, there should be an upper limit on the differences in position between the detected robot and the estimate.
This should help filter out some false positions

issue_title: Move beluga.py from main package to driver or new core package
issue_contents: Having beluga.py in beluga_main creates circular dependency with swarm_simulator as they each depend on eachother.

issue_title: Beluga Driver Documentation
issue_contents: Complete documentation for mainpage and for Teleop nodes in the beluga_driver package.

issue_title: Missing miabot_sim.py node
issue_contents: Not sure if this got accidentally deleted or if it was never created. Either way, for the simulation of the ROS system to work, it needs to be there.

issue_title: In miabot_module, button does not turn yellow on click
issue_contents: The connect button should turn yellow on click and then change red/green when action is complete. Should be yellow during action. The GUI doesn't refresh on 'button.setStyleSheet('QPushButton {color: yellow}')'
Figure out how to force refresh or thread send goal on separate process.

issue_title: MiabotPlugin has attributes that should be private
Attributes in MiabotNode are public that should be private
issue_contents: All attributes of the MiabotNode class in dcsl_miabot_node.py should be change to lead with an underscore "_" to denote private.

issue_title: Vision tracker fails with no background images present.
issue_contents: Vision tracker will not properly initialize without background images on system.
Would prevent user from generating new backgrounds on fresh install.

issue_contents: I'm running this package under  Ubuntu 14.04 using ros indigo.

As well as Freiburg101_scan although works with the default parameters:
Freigbrug52 worked though with 2.5m but the result looks weird
So I guess I'm doing something wrong while using this. What do I need to do to run this exact same tests as in the paper published at ICRA2017 ?

issue_title: Node graph for generating and modifying signals, and manipulating images/textures
issue_contents: The signal generation doesn't need to run on the gpu, at least not for the very simple signal generation initially.
But image adding/subtracting/multiplying does need to run on the gpu.
Each node requires the set shader call, and all the input and output textures to be bound, and uniforms to be set.
The loaded shader then processes the inputs and updates the outputs.
It would make sense to organize all the nodes by type if changing shaders is assumed to be the most expensive operation.
Every update uses the textures/inputs from t-1 and outputs on the current texture.

As long as no two nodes are outputting on the same texture this assures no conflicts- this should be an error anyhow, if not prevented the texture may flicker back and forth, or the output from the earlier computation may be never seen/used at all because it is always overwritten by the later.
Every value/texture only propagates one node per update.
vimjay had a back propagation approach that only updated nodes feeding into outputs, and inputs could traverse the entire graph from start to end in one update - maybe either is desirable.
Also look at https://github.com/CedricGuillemet/Imogen  - doesn't build on Linux but probably could with a little work.

issue_title: Cubemap camera with normal map lens for arbitrary lenses
issue_contents: Need to render a cube map from the camera perspective.
Any physical or non physical lens can be approximated with a properly generated normal map-
Every pixel location would define the direction that pixel is looking, which could be completely backwards.
A square (of two triangles) needs to be passed into the vertex shader in order to get the uv look up coords for the output fragments.
This allows cylindrical and spherical lenses and very strange lenses with different parts pointing in different directions.
The normal map could be supplied via a ros topic, or added via addTexture.
Alternatively an arbitrary shape could be generated whose normals define where to do the lookup into the cubemap,
and floats in front of a regular camera.
The shape could be a rectangle but the normals would capture the shape of the lens,
and opengl would interpolate the normals for the fragment shader-
it wouldn't be up to the user to define a normal for every pixel
(though a very low resolution normal map could be provided and the interpolation still happens there).

For effiiciency it could be determined whether a cube face has no pixels on it at all (don't render it) or only partial coverage (only render that part - maybe per pixel or just a bounding rectangle).
May need to dynamically resize cube faces pixel dimensions based on aov and which faces are covered.

issue_title: Mirrors for objects, projectors, and lights
issue_contents: Only 1 level deep- don't have mirrors reflecting mirrors.
Could handle with a Camera that renders to a flat surface where the mirror is:
compute where the camera should be given the position of the viewer,
then render the scene from that location taking into account the aov limitation of the size of the mirror
and a resolution determined by the resolution of the viewer and the distance to the mirror.
It would be easy to disable after that in cpu computation if the mirror is out of view.
Lights need to be duplicated across the mirror but not illuminate anything outside of the aov defined by the distance of the light to the mirror and the angle it hits.
Projectors may be the most tricky, need to find the corners of the projected texture on the surface of the mirror,
then create a new projector that projects that chunk in the reflected direction.
Use mostly cpu methods at first but later look at offloading to gpu shaders.

issue_title: updateLinks() been commented inside its caller addNDTGraph()
issue_contents: Functions (int) AutoCompleteGraphLocalization::createNewLinks() and (inline void) AutoCompleteGraphBase::updateLinks() has been fully commented inside the source code.

A member function (int) createNewLinks() of class AutoCompleteGraph calls addLinkBetweenMaps(vec, *it_prior, *it) . Then only one function with the same name  AutoCompleteGraphLocalization::addLinkBetweenMaps() can be found, which tells  "Those links are not usable anymore in Localization. Use AutoCompleteGraph for that".

The member function  createNewLinks() of class AutoCompleteGraph is only called by (virtual void) updateLinks(), a member function of class AutoCompleteGraphFeature inherited from class AutoCompleteGraph. Yet the only call to updateLinks() is commented inside its caller AutoCompleteGraphLocalization::addNDTGraph().
The Auto-Complete Graph paper is scientifically solid and the source is well organized. Hope these tiny puzzles can soon be resolved.

issue_title: graph_map ROS package and related ROS messages are needed

issue_contents: I'm working with ROS2 and attempting to replicate **_a setup that works correctly in ROS1_**: launching multiple instances of SITL (ArduPilot Copter v4.5.7) and MAVROS2 on the same PC for multi-UAV simulation.
When I launch multiple instances (between 4 to 7) of SITL + MAVROS2 simultaneously on an Intel i7-12700H (20 threads), CPU usage spikes close to 100% in every core.

issue_title: ROS1 Mavros global_position plugin not publishing fused global position topics unless number of satellites >= 15
issue_contents: In my ros1 & px4 project I've experienced that mavros only publishes the fused global position topics `~/global`, `~/local`, `~/rel_alt` & `~/compass_hdg` if the number of satellites visible is greater or equal to 15, despite correctly interpreting the mavlink data which is also getting published on the `raw/fix` topic.

Despite being in a relatively large field near a lake, during my flight tests if the weather is clear and I'm lucky I can sometimes get 15-20 visible satellites, however on cloudy days or just 'bad' days in general, I usually hover around 10 satellites with a 1 - 1.5 `hdop`/`vdop`. I'm wondering if this is desired behaviour or if I'm missing something, as I've read through the documentation and the [global_position.cpp file](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/master/mavros/src/plugins/global_position.cpp), none of which state a required number of satellites beyond that of px4's internal required default `6` satellites in order to take off. Not only does my code expect msgs over the `~/global` topic but also it expects a transform being published between the `map` and `base_link` frames which again is only published to `/tf` when the number of visible satellites >=15. For the time being I'm going to create a new node that reads the incoming msgs from the `~/raw/fix` topic and forward it to the `~/global` topic and `/tf` if the number of visible satellites is under 15 satellites, if that's not a good solution then I am all ears for a better stopgap or permanent fix.

issue_title: MavROS populates global_position/compass_hdg with ARHS heading instead of compass data
issue_contents: The MAVRos global position plugin supports a channel called `global_position/compass_hdg`.
In the docs, it calls this `Compass heading in degrees.` and populates the heading into a `std_msgs/msg/Float64`
This is not a compass heading. This is the vehicle's AHRS heading.
Just reading the docs, I would expect the heading from the primary compass, in either true heading or magnetic heading.
I believe this is misleading, and either the implementation should change, or the docs should change.

In the event the vehicle's EKF diverges but the compass sensor still works, now the ROS algorithm you thought was using compass sensor heading is actually using a diverged state estimate from what the sensor is reporting. This interface also does not populate the uncertainty of the value, so if the EKF variances are high there is no way to know whether to trust this value. Overall, I am not sure why this message exists.

issue_title: Serial port baud rates are dependent and restricted by the version of asio
issue_contents: Serial port baud rates are dependent and restricted by the version of asio. Particularly, in the serial_port_base.ipp some baud rates might be missing but still supported by the OS with termios/termios2/ioctl. In my case, it is the 1500000 baud rate which throws the Device exceptio within MAVROS but works fine if set manually. In the latest asio master it is still missing.

A proposed solution might be to split the try-catch in the serial device constructor into sections and try one more time with serial_dev.native_handle() and ioctl if the baud rate option causes an exception.

issue_title: Inquiry Regarding Coordinate Systems and Roll/Pitch Commands in Gazebo/SITL Simulation
issue_contents: I am currently working on a university project focused on the implementation and testing of a fixed-wing guidance algorithm in the Gazebo/SITL simulation environment, using the Arduplane control platform. Additionally, I am using the ROS platform and the MAVROS package to receive controller messages and send commands to the fixed-wing UAV.

Based on my initial research into the coordinate systems used in MAVROS, it appears that the package employs the ENU (East-North-Up) coordinate system for sending roll and pitch reference commands to Arduplane. These commands are sent through the "/mavros/setpoint_raw/attitude" topic.

I have implemented a two-dimensional guidance algorithm accordingly and tested its output by sending it to the SITL simulation via the aforementioned tools. However, based on the simulation results in Gazebo, the fixed-wing UAV exhibits unusual behavior, particularly with constant oscillations around the roll axis.
I would greatly appreciate your guidance in addressing the following questions:
What coordinate systems are used in SITL/Gazebo simulation and the ROS package for sending and receiving commands and messages?

In which coordinate system should the output of my guidance algorithm, which provides roll, pitch, and thrust references for the inner loop, be computed? Additionally, is the topic I am using suitable for sending these commands?
Thank you in advance for your time and assistance. I look forward to your valuable insights.

issue_title: Persistent network disconnection causes a crash
issue_contents: When running mavros via UDP and a network/radio disconnection event occurs, an intended retry in the [libmavconn udp.cpp](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/ros2/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp) file can cause unintended, potentially dangerous behaviour.

In the `libmavconn/src/udp.cpp` `send_message()` function, MAVROS is using boost's IO Service ([specifically uses post() on lines 249](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/97cf3c606197d2e5ee83d1b8896e135db6bd649a/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp#L249) & 275) to make an async call of `do_sendto()`. The [do_sento()](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/97cf3c606197d2e5ee83d1b8896e135db6bd649a/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp#L304) function uses `async_send_to()` from the `boost ip::udp::socket` class to read from a message queue and send the data to an endpoint. During a prolonged network disconnection, the system can crash.

When there is a network/radio disconnection during message transmission, `async_send_to()` returns an `asio::error::network_unreachable` error. This error is caught on [line 324](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/97cf3c606197d2e5ee83d1b8896e135db6bd649a/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp#L324) where the issue is logged. For this particular type of error, the function does not return. Rather, the function continues to run and there is a comment in the code indicating that this is intended:

Since the message queue is not empty, execution continues. Since the network is disconnected, [no bytes are transferred and the position in the message buffer is not modified](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/97cf3c606197d2e5ee83d1b8896e135db6bd649a/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp#L343C7-L343C40). Execution continues to [line 348](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/97cf3c606197d2e5ee83d1b8896e135db6bd649a/libmavconn/src/udp.cpp#L348), in which `do_sendto()` is recursively called. If the network does not reestablish, this causes a loop in which `async_send_to()` continues to error out with `asio::error::network_unreachable` and without any data being transmitted. This recalling of `do_sendto()` will loop continuously and basically hang. Eventually, the recursive mutex will reach the maximum number of locks that can be applied which will cause a crash, or, if we continue to call `send_message()`, other threads will wait until the recursive mutex is unlocked which will never happen. This will cause all threads to hang until eventually we run out of available threads.
If there is any misunderstanding in the behaviour of this function on my end, please let me know.
Is this an intentional design choice for Mavros?
Is there a better/safer way to handle this particular issue when the radio fails without continually waiting and crashing?

issue_contents: Finding information for MAVROS2 has been pretty frustrating as relevant information seems scarce.
As much as I have struggled to get some of this working, I would be more than happy to write up some tutorials after all of this.
The best source of information I've found came from this post [here](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/issues/1718).
From this, I have been attempting to manually deploy the commands to a Pixhawk FMU via a rpi companion computer using a combination of services and especially commandLong, i.e. for arming:

I later realized you must also follow your firmware's documentation as well, and the supported parameters found [here](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/mavlink-get-set-flightmode.html) for ardupilot, thus the values for param1 and param2.
I can confirm the mode is being set in mission planner flight modes tab.

Since I was able to get those working, I have tried working through other commands found in the mavlink [docs](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html) and then crossreferencing those with ardupilot documentation.
However, all other commands I've tested have failed.

With broadcast set to false, nothing happens/no output. Setting broadcast to true shows "Unexpected command 22, result 4" I have all of the prearm safety checks unchecked, other than the hardware button found on my gps unit.
Trying the built in mavros service for taking off:
this gives success=false result=4, which according to mavlink docs, 4 means good command but failed to execute, as in the prior method.

My goal is to implement all of the guided commands found [here](https://ardupilot.org/dev/docs/copter-commands-in-guided-mode.html) programatically. Some of these fall under the message category, not the command category on mavlink docs, which commandLong I assume is only for the command category.

I assume some of these commands are built into the other mavros services, but as I cannot find any documentation on how to use them, it has really been a game of trial and error on using just the commandLong.

If someone could point me in the right direction on either finding documentation on some of the mavros services or figuring out how to implement some of these commands and messages found in mavlink/ardupilot documentation that would be greatly appreciated.
Ubuntu: 22.04.2 LTS (in docker container running on raspberry pi bullseye)

issue_title: Possible error in imu.cpp plugin code
issue_contents: Hello, I think there may be an error in the code that handles the scaled IMU message. In the mavlink website you can see that the scaled IMU message contains the magnetic field data in mgauss. But the code for the plugin uses a coeff of 1000.0 and it's called MILLIT_TO_TESLA, as it if was interpreting that the data was in mtesla instead of mgauss.
So naturally when I check the topic on ROS I get my magnetic field data in mgauss multiplied by 1000.0, which is clearly wrong as it's supposed to show in Tesla according to the ROS documentation.

Also I should mention that in the same code the _publish_imu_data_raw_ function is used for the scaled IMU instead of the _publish_imu_data_ one that is also there. So when I check my topics I have to go to _/mavros/imu/data_raw_ when it should be _/mavros/imu/data_.
If this is indeed an error I would appreciate that it would get fixed in the source as we are trying to avoid to create our own package for the project I'm working on.
Thanks in advance for your consideration.

issue_title: waypoint JSON null converted to 0
issue_contents: JSON files save NaN as null, so when you create a mission that has no waypoint headings (param4 = NaN), it gets saved as 'null' in the JSON. When loading this again and uploading to the drone using waypointPush, this null gets converted to 0, meaning the drone flies the whole mission pointing North.

I can fix this by checking for null in every parameter of every waypoint and converting to NaN before pushing, but it took me a while to figure out what the problem was, and I feel like this should be built into MAVROS.
I used to work with MAVROS <-> Ardupilot, and I don't remember this being an issue - it seems to only be an issue with MAVROS <-> PX4.
In this console output snippet, I upload the mission file using QGC and you can see it has nans. Then I load the same file using rosnodejs and push with MAVROS, and the nans are 0s.

issue_title: MAVROS: Local Map Frame Axes Mismatch
issue_contents: Hi guys. I have been trying to use mavros with pixhawk cube orange. However, I'm facing issues with frame conversions. I know that pixhawk autopilot uses NED frame. Mavros by convention uses ENU but according to REP 103, ROS uses NWU as default frame. For NWU frame moving forward is positive +X and moving left is positive +Y. However, when I move pixhawk cube orange forward, the position values in mavros (from topic /mavros/local_position/pose) decreases in the Y direction. When I move to the left, the position values increases in X. When I replace my cube orange with a pixhawk 4, my axes are oriented correctly w.r.t. NWU in mavros. The problem seems to be specific to my pixhawk cube orange.
Update: While calibrating the compass in QGC with pixhawk firmware, it shows external compass rotation: ROTATION_ROLL_180_YAW_90. Do you think the axes mismatch is because of this?

issue_title: Getting local pose in multi-UAV simulation
issue_contents: I'm running multi-UAV simulation via `roslaunch px4 multi_uav_mavros_sitl.launch`. I'm used to using `/local_position/pose` to provide feedback for a tracking controller. However, at simulation start, the local position readouts from each of `/uav[012]/mavros/local_position` are close to [0; 0; 0] as shown below. This runs contrary to the expected positions of each uav specified in `multi_uav_mavros_sitl.launch`, i.e. [0,0,0] for uav0, [1,0,0] for uav1, [0,1,0] for uav2

I am aware that `local_position` is computed with respected to some global frame (named `map` ??). What I assume now is that each UAV's `local_position/pose` is calculated w.r.t. its own global frame, whose origin is set to its own position at simulation start. The issue now is whether it is possible to calculate every UAV's local position in the same, global, frame. I have attempted to use `/mavros/cmd/set_home`, to no effect.

Writing a frame transformation function to resolve every UAV's pose in the same frame appears to be feasible, but I still hope that mavros provides this functionality so i don't need to code myself :)

issue_title: Fake GPS Velocity Frame Issue
issue_contents: We are using fake GPS on PX4 and noticed that we get drift and high velocity residuals. We are still testing further, but suspect these lines. The velocity is calculated using a single step finite difference approximation. vel = ([pos[t_1] - pos[t_0]) / dt. The problem is that the frame is incorrect. These positions are in earth centered, earth fixed coordinates. This is not the north east down coordinate system. As soon as we move from hover, our residuals spike. We will submit a patch after test flying it.

issue_title: mavros_msgs HILGPS message documentation contradiction
issue_contents: The documentation for [MAVROS HILGPS](http://docs.ros.org/en/api/mavros_msgs/html/msg/HilGPS.html) references the [MAVLINK documentation for HILGPS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#HIL_GPS) but does not conform to the same SI units as MAVLINK. I understand that ROS implements[ REP103](https://www.ros.org/reps/rep-0103.html) and [REP105](https://www.ros.org/reps/rep-0105.html) for unit standards but this is extremely confusing when the referenced documentation states otherwise and can (and has...) result in an aircraft crashing when using HILGPS in a GPS assisted mode. An example of these unit differences are
**Parameter  /  MAVLINK Defined SI Unit   /  MAVROS Required SI Unit**
Add comment in [mavros_msgs/HilGPS](http://docs.ros.org/en/api/mavros_msgs/html/msg/HilGPS.html) documentation to state the units to be used for these parameters.

issue_title: Possibility of creating additional Mavros topics for different Mavlink messages?
issue_contents: I'm not sure if this is something that already exists, or if it is possible/feasible to implement within mavros, but I am working with gimbal controls in a ROS2 environment.  I've been able to publish commands to simulation successfully to control the gimbal, but a lot of the gimbal specific information I need access to is not currently (readably) exposed through an existing mavros topic.  I'm not sure if there is some functionality already within mavros that I can take advantage of to get/translate the data from the relevant Mavlink messages.

I've been able to determine that the messages are being received and republished in the ROS topic `/uas1/mavlink_source` (I collected the messages simply through the terminal using `ros2 topic echo /uas1/mavlink_source | egrep -B 14 -A 14 "msgid: XXX"`).  I assume that mavros is already already doing some very similar message translation in creating the existing topics for things like GPS data, altitude, etc.  I'm wondering if there is some way to add additional messages (specifically by id, and likely defining the payload of data contained within somehow) and create topics for the contents of those messages from Mavlink, and how I would go about setting this up.

I think it is likely that mavros will likely include these messages in the future, as the previous method of gimbal control which was included in mavros 1 (mavros/mavros_extras/src/plugins/mount_control.cpp) is now deprecated (see [here](https://mavlink.io/en/services/gimbal_v2.html) for the documentation I used in constructing my commands for gimbal control/understanding the messages/commands being used now which replaced those used by mount_control).  At this point I don't necessarily need all of the functionality which was provided by the mount_control plugin, but I do need access to the gimbal state being published to Mavlink.
Here are the messages which are relevant to gimbal control (there may be more, but these are the ones that I came across):

If anyone could point me in the right direction for either decoding the message and its payload manually or using some functionality within mavros to assist so I can get it published to a topic alongside the rest of the mavros data that would be greatly appreciated!
Version: Through Auterion suite simulator, software release v2.3.1

As a final note, it might be useful (though I'm not sure how feasible) to add functionality for [MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE) to return messages in a useful, translated/readable way, as currently calling that message through the generic CommandLong doesn't return the message but just says whether or not requesting it was successful.  It does however publish that message to `/uas1/mavlink_source` in the untranslated format identifiable by the msgid.
contents_details: [GIMBAL_DEVICE_ATTITUDE_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GIMBAL_DEVICE_ATTITUDE_STATUS) - msgid: 283
This message (should) include the gimbal orientation within the q field and is published frequently and seen in  `/uas1/mavlink_source` in my simulation environment

This is also the only message I definitely need access to for the project I'm working on, as the default gimbal_device_id worked for requesting control, but I still need the real-time information about the gimbal's orientation.
[GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GIMBAL_MANAGER_INFORMATION) - msgid: 280
This message contains the information used to identify the gimbal you're requesting control of (gimbal_device_id) as well as its capabilities and maximum angles.
This message is documented to be requested by the ground station using MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE but in my sim it was being published regularly as well.
[GIMBAL_MANAGER_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#GIMBAL_MANAGER_STATUS) - msgid: 281

This message indicates the gimbal manager flags as well as primary and secondary control sysid and compid for the respective gimbal_device_id, which you would need to alter to take control of the gimbal from within mavros.

When requesting control of the gimbal from the ros terminal, you need to use the compid of the onboard computer as it is used by the mavros UAS node.  I found this (mostly by accident) while looking through the mavros source code in `/mavros/mavros/include/mavros/mavros_uas.hpp` and it is 191, this is also documented in mavlink as the primary onboard computer's compid.  The command I used is as follows:
`ros2 service call /mavros/cmd/command mavros_msgs/srv/CommandLong "{command: 1001, param1: -2, param2: 191, param3: -1, param4: -1, param7: 154}"`

The command code is for [MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE), default gimbal_device_id is 154 and passed to param7 while the compid is passed to param2.
`ros2 service call /mavros/cmd/command mavros_msgs/srv/CommandLong "{command: 1000, param1: -40, param2: -90, param3: -0.3, param4: -0.3, param7: 154}"`
[MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW)

issue_title: setpoint_raw velocity setpoint not behaving as expected
issue_contents: This is only bug and feature tracker, please use it
to report bugs or request features.

We have developed a system using mavros as the core for providing control to our quadcopter platform. During operation in Offboard, we are sending messages to the setpoint_raw/local topic with as either positional (XYZ) or velocity setpoints (using positional Z to maintain altitude).

When transmitting velocity setpoints, the drone does not behave as I expect. For example, when publishing a desired setpoint of 1.0 m/s in the Y direction (corresponding to forward) I would expect the drone to increase/decrease its pitch angle in order to maintain the desired velocity. However, if the external forces are applied to the drone (i.e wind) the flight controller does not seem to compensate in order to achieve the 1.0 m/s desired by the companion computer setpoints.

The measured velocity of the drone is taken from the "/mavros/local_position/velocity_body/ " topic, with setpoints being sent across the "/mavros/setpoint_raw/local" topic. An example setpoint message can be seen below:

Have I got my assumptions wrong about velocity set points, or should it be noted that I have to implement some kind of PID loop to adjust the input to ensure our drone meets the desired 1.5 m/s velocity?

issue_contents: @vooon  @TSC21 Hello.I have been receiving error "REQUEST FAILED CHECK MAVROS LOGS" while running command "rosrun mavros mavsafety arm".

I am able to arm the apm2.6 with TX RX but with mavros arming it shows error and does not arm.
I think there might be some problem with tgt_system and tgt_component values which by default are set to 1.
With these values only mavsys -c STABILIZE works and when i try different values of above two params then mavsys stabilize also begins to show error of request failed.
Its been a long time working over this problem but could not find any solution.

issue_title: Add support for Windows & OSX
issue_contents: As part of the RoboStack project, we are aiming to provide cross-platform ROS packages that can be installed via conda (see https://github.com/RoboStack/ros-noetic). We were able to successfully compile mavros on Linux, macOS & Windows.
For Windows (which I know is currently not supported by mavros), we needed quite a few patches to get mavros to compile. macOS was much easier. You can see the patches here:

Are you interested at all in merging these patches upstream? Most of the patches could be easily guarded by `if(WIN)` type statements (and most of them are already). For example, I did not find a simple equivalent for `set_this_thread_name` and would simply disable that on Windows. Other changes are a little more annoying - I needed to move some variables from being private/protected to public, as the Visual Studio compiler complained about trying to access these which is not allowed (I am not sure about the C++ internals, and why it works on Linux but not Windows).
contents_details: [libmavconn](https://github.com/RoboStack/ros-noetic/blob/master/patch/ros-noetic-libmavconn.win.patch)
[mavlink](https://github.com/RoboStack/ros-noetic/blob/master/patch/ros-noetic-mavlink.patch) - this includes some conda specific patches around PYHONEXECUTABLE, please ignore these
[mavros-1](https://github.com/RoboStack/ros-noetic/blob/master/patch/ros-noetic-mavros.patch) - this includes a patch that is required for both Windows and macOS

[mavros-2](https://github.com/RoboStack/ros-noetic/blob/master/patch/ros-noetic-mavros.win.patch) - this includes a bunch of patches for Windows specifically, and in the current state would break the other platforms (we only apply this patch on Windows).

issue_title: [libmavconn] tcp client/server illegal thread join from io_thread itself
issue_contents: This is an issue when the server closes with an established connection, it causes a terminate on the client.
`io_thread` runs the `io_service` which runs things like `do_recv`, `do_send` (for the TCPClient, but the Server has a similar issue).

In these async methods, any failure (including EOF i.e. the server going offline) calls `close()` on the client, which joins the `io_thread`. That means the `io_thread` is getting joined from the thread itself, which throws (see error conditions in https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/thread/thread/join)
Moving the `join()` to the destructors of Client/Server seems to solve the issue.
This then allows the main program to get the `port_closed_cb` and do a reconnection routine, without terminating.

issue_title: The doc of mavros_msgs about coordinate needs better clarification.
issue_contents: Mavros takes care of the transforms between the two frames.
So if you want to send a setpoint to the FCU, it must be defined in ENU frame (X forward and Z up), Mavros will do the transform in NED coordinates.
Conversely when you want to read the current pose of the quadrotor, you can use mavros/local_position/pose, mavros will do the transformation so that you will read the pose in ENU as well
While in the documentation in http://docs.ros.org/en/api/mavros_msgs/html/msg/PositionTarget.html, FRAME_LOCAL_NED and FRAME_BODY_NED are still used. It can misguide many beginners of mavros like me.
So I suggest to rename these FRAM CONSTANT like this:
issue_quotes: the FCU is working with the NED frame and ROS is working with the ENU frame.

issue_title: Modify Geofence via Mavros Interface?
issue_contents: I would like to specify a geofence for my drone from its onboard companion computer. There I have a ROS node, that takes care of the mission control and interfaces to the FCU via mavros. I would like to specify a geofence from within that node during flight, based on sensor data that is processed on the companion.
In the docs I didn't find a plugin for this, mavros_msgs doesn't seem to contain the relevant messages and services, so I assume that this functionality does not yet exist.
I only found this related feature request: https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/issues/1157
Has anyone dealt with this before (and can share any workarounds)? Did anyone make progress implementing this?

issue_title: How local_position measured when using optical flow and distance sensor
issue_contents: I am curious how local_position is measured when using optical flow as the positioning system. I know there is no reliable position data in x and y directions. However, I think the orientation and height should be correct. But it is not true in my case. I checked the output using `rostopic echo mavros/local_position/pose`, the orientation is good, but the local z is wrong and it is varying, the range can be from 0.67-1. And my "rostopic echo mavros/distance_sensor/hrlv_ez4.pub" can give the correct estimation. I changed the "EKF2_HGT_MODE" to range sensor but it still gives the strange reading on local.pose.pose.z. So I am wondering how local_position is implemented when using optical flow as the guidance system. Thanks.

issue_title: Yaw setpoint changing unexpectedly
issue_contents: When using `setpoint_position/local` and then `setpoint_velocity/cmd_vel_unstamped` to control the position and velocity of the drone respectively, the yaw setpoint drifts away from the constant value that was set when publishing the pose command, even though we're commanding an [X, Y, Z] angular twist of [0, 0, 0].

If you take a look at the rosbag and the PX4 flight log, you can see that when we stop publishing to `setpoint_position/local` and start publishing to `setpoint_velocity/cmd_vel_unstamped` that the yaw setpoint is no longer constant, and the drone moves accordingly when we expect it not to.

issue_title: distance_sensor publisher. Incorrect orientation on the ROS side
issue_contents: The distance_sensor plugin reads orientation of rangefinder from mavlink message and this orientation is used for sending TF. But it is assumed that orientation in mavlink message is valid for NED frame not front-left-up. In case of ArduCopter, if parameter RNGFND1_ORIENT set to 25 (Down), in rviz rangefinder will be directed up.

issue_title: Jerky Autonomous navigation following a manual flight log
issue_contents: What is the best way to follow a manual flight as closely as possible?
Right now I’m sending every 'n' points from a manual flight local log (x,y,z, yaw, and velocities) to `/mavros/setpoint_raw/local `with `mavros_msgs::PositionTarget` messages.

This roughly works, but between every setpoint, it slows down and speeds up again (I’m guessing due to the PID), and this causes the motion to be super jerky. Is there any solution for this, or a better way to do this?

P.S. I’m running all this with gazebo, and not actual hardware, and I eventually want to do this in GPS denied environments, so I’m not sure if I could use the mavros waypoint mission since it requires lat,long,alt.

issue_title: Local position plugin not accounting for translational offset to "map" frame?
issue_contents: Maybe I'm missing something (definitely possible) - but it seems that the mavros local position is published with (converted to ENU) values directly from the local position mavlink message from PX4, however, defining these values as within the "map" frame, which as I understand it, is defined with **origin at home position**, which is offset translationally from the actual PX4 local position origin (defined in the GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN msg).
Is there something going on behind the scene that I am not seeing with the tf's? Or is this a bug?
Mavros frame logic described in the global position plugin here: https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/a1dd03c6db26107f914b4526305abca9733f7486/mavros/src/plugins/global_position.cpp#L329-L333

issue_title: Running precision landing on the FCU with landing target plugin doesn't seem to be working
issue_contents: I am working on a precision landing problem where I have a custom vision node ([aruco_detect](https://github.com/UbiquityRobotics/fiducials)) that runs on the companion computer (Ubuntu 16.04, ROS Kinetic) and passes the pose estimation to the [landing_target.cpp plugin](https://github.com/mavlink/mavros/blob/master/mavros_extras/src/plugins/landing_target.cpp). The message type that I'm using is PoseStamped ([geometry_msgs::PoseStamped](http://docs.ros.org/melodic/api/geometry_msgs/html/msg/PoseStamped.html)) msg. I added a few print statements into landing_target.cpp and captured a snapshot of the data that the plugin is receiving.

When I'm testing, the drone arms, switches to the GUIDED mode, and takes off to 3m, then it flies over the aruco marker. I monitor the output of the vision node and when it starts publishing the pose estimation (a marker is being detected), the drone switches to the land mode and lands. I expect the drone to follow the landing target that is set while it's descending, which doesn't appear to be the case. It looks like it doesn't take corrective actions and instead it lands where it is.

issue_title: global_position/local wrong value in x direction
issue_contents: we are working on implementing the Marvelmind positioning system for indoor flying. Everything is working just fine, the only issue we are facing is that when echoing global_position/local the x direction (East West) is off (for each meter moved according to the rostopic we move 1.49m in real life). The y and z axis are accurate. Tracking in the Marvelmind system is stable and accurate and we are streaming the position data to APM via NMEA. We have the suspicion that the problem is caused by the coordinate frame we are using and the longitude we are at (50°N) is causing this error. We are using the global_position/local topic to define our waypoints measured from the home position. When executing our control program in SITL it has no effect on our waypoint mission (e.g. flying a square). When flying in real life the drone is flying in a rectangle. We simply don't know what configuration step we are missing in order to fix the x direction.
Any help fixing this problem is greatly appreciated.

issue_title: Reading original RC transmitter Signal when using OverrideRCIn
issue_contents: Just wondering if someone could help me better understand the **rc_io mavros** topics. My goal is to be able to read in RC signals from the rc transmitter and be able to modify them if needed. Right now I read the RC signals from the rc transmitter by subscribing to **/mavros/rc/in** topic. This works well. Next, if I need to override any RC channel I simply publish the value for the channel on **/mavros/rc/override**. When I do so, I can see that the **/mavros/rc/in** values change to reflect the override value. The problem is that when I override the value, on the next loop iteration, whenever I read the rc transmitter value again I will be seeing the override value that I put in instead of the original rc signal (not overridden). This puts my reading/processing logic in a state of continuously reading myself whenever I try to modify the signal. I need to be able to distinguish between the original signal and the override.
Is there a way to always read the original rc signal of the rc transmitter before it gets overidden?

to report bugs or request features.
_Please describe the problem, or desired feature_
1.I'm able to list topics from the FCU.
2.At this stage when I echo /diagnostics it says FCU Connected.
3.To subscribe to topics I need to change the stream rate using rosservice command to 10 Hz
4.After this the /diagnostics says the FCU is not connected and thus I cant subscribe to topics published by mavros

issue_title: Comunication problem pixhawk, arducopter, mavros 0.32
issue_contents: I have a pixhawk 1 connected through an ftdi adapter (chines clone) to an odroid xu4 runing ubuntu 16.04 and mavros 0.32 from binary. I've tried with 115200, 921600 and the problem is always the same, I have heartbeat but don't receive several ros topics (/mavros/imu/data, /mavros/battery....) after some time I have CON Lost message. I've tested with a desktop PC too and the same problem. I add some details info

issue_title: Turn UAV to the specified point with /mission/push  service and Wp index out of bounds error
issue_contents: This is only bug and feature tracker, please use it
to report bugs or request features.

I want to send the uav tool to the latitude longitude altitute coordinates I specified. İn this reason I used /mavros/mission/push service. UAV goes to coordinates I specified but moves back or sideways to 2nd coordinate point. After turning the UAV to the specified point, I want it to go to that point. Can I do this with the / mavros / mission / push service? or how do I do it?

Finally, I get "wp index out of bounds" error when I run node. For now, it did not adversely affect the execution of the code. I don't know what the error is, how it affects the system, how to solve it.
Mavros: ros-kinetic-mavros is already the newest version

issue_title: Security issue and digital sky compliance
issue_contents: The new rules of Digital sky in India requires a secure communication of at least 128bit encryption even while using wire between FCU and companion computer. Also there is a requirement of Detect and avoid(DAA) which is comparatively easy to develop on ROS. And there is a need for specific type of flight logs with geofencing breach and time limit breach etc. in json format. Mavros with secured connection can then be used to develop flight logs as well as pacify the development of DAA.

Mavlink 2 looks like it has secured signing but due to some reasons it has not been implemented on Mavros. Are there any plans to make to secure the serial line or is there any other branch that already supports it?
